$comment: Licence posture checks. Titles, minimums and fixes are Vigil365's own words. Baseline references are identifiers only: SCuBA IDs from CISA ScubaGear (CC0, see baselineSources). CIS recommendation numbers stay empty until CIS's licence terms are checked, and Secure Score control names stay empty until verified (docs/LICENSE_POSTURE_PLAN.md section 6). 'reads' is where the evidence comes from: graph, or exchange (Exchange Online PowerShell, phase 2).

checks.title: Conditional Access requires MFA for all users
checks.whyItMatters: A password alone is the most common way into a Microsoft 365 tenant. A policy that asks everyone for a second factor stops most of those sign-ins.
checks.minimum: An enabled Conditional Access policy for all users that requires MFA or an authentication strength.
fix: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open Conditional Access and create a policy for all users and all resources.
Grant access only with multifactor authentication, and exclude two break-glass accounts.
Turn it on in report-only first, check the sign-in logs, then switch it to On.

checks.title: Legacy authentication is blocked
checks.whyItMatters: Old sign-in protocols can't do MFA, so attackers use them to try stolen passwords without being challenged.
checks.minimum: An enabled Conditional Access policy for all users that blocks Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients.
fix: Create a Conditional Access policy for all users and all resources.
Under Conditions, Client apps, select Exchange ActiveSync clients and Other clients.
Set Grant to Block access, test in report-only, then turn it on.

checks.title: MFA is enforced by Security Defaults or Conditional Access
checks.whyItMatters: Every tenant can enforce MFA at no extra cost. Without Security Defaults or a Conditional Access policy, nobody is asked for a second factor.
checks.minimum: Security Defaults on, or a Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for all users.
fix: With Microsoft Entra ID P1, use Conditional Access (see 'Conditional Access requires MFA for all users').
Without it, turn on Security Defaults in the Microsoft Entra admin center, under Overview, Properties.

checks.title: At least 95% of users are registered for MFA
checks.whyItMatters: A user who never registered a second factor can't be protected by MFA, and the first person to register it may be an attacker.
checks.minimum: 95% or more of member users registered for MFA.
fix: Run a registration campaign in the Microsoft Entra admin center, under Authentication methods.
Follow up with the users listed on Vigil365's Identity page.

checks.title: High-risk users and sign-ins are blocked
checks.whyItMatters: Microsoft scores users and sign-ins that look compromised. Blocking the high-risk ones stops an attacker who already has the password.
checks.minimum: Enabled Conditional Access policies that block high user risk and high sign-in risk.
fix: Create a Conditional Access policy for all users with User risk set to High, and Grant set to Block.
Create a second policy with Sign-in risk set to High, and Grant set to Block.

checks.title: Admin roles are granted just in time with PIM
checks.whyItMatters: Permanent admin rights are a standing target. With PIM, admins activate a role only when they need it, for a limited time.
checks.minimum: Highly privileged roles have eligible assignments in PIM and no permanent active ones.
fix: In Privileged Identity Management, make admins eligible for their roles instead of permanently active.
Require approval to activate Global Administrator.

checks.title: Intune has a device compliance policy
checks.whyItMatters: Compliance policies define what a healthy device is. Without one, Conditional Access can't tell a managed, patched laptop from any other.
checks.minimum: At least one device compliance policy.
fix: In the Intune admin center, open Devices, Compliance, and create a policy for each platform in use.
Then require a compliant device in Conditional Access for the apps that matter.

checks.title: External sharing is limited to existing guests
checks.whyItMatters: When anyone can be sent a link, files can leave the organisation with no sign-in and no record of who opened them.
checks.minimum: SharePoint and OneDrive sharing set to existing guests or people in the organisation only.
fix: In the SharePoint admin center, open Policies, Sharing.
Set the SharePoint and OneDrive sharing level to Existing guests or Only people in your organization.

checks.title: Safe Links protects all users
checks.whyItMatters: Safe Links checks a link when it's clicked, not just when the email arrives, so a link that turns malicious later is still caught.
checks.minimum: A Safe Links policy, or the Standard or Strict preset, applied to all recipients.
fix: In Microsoft Defender, open Email & collaboration, Policies & rules, Threat policies.
Turn on the Standard preset security policy for all recipients, or create a Safe Links policy for all recipient domains.

checks.title: Preset security policies are turned on
checks.whyItMatters: The Standard and Strict presets apply Microsoft's recommended email protection in one step and keep it current as Microsoft updates it.
checks.minimum: The Standard or Strict preset security policy applied to all recipients.
fix: In Microsoft Defender, open Email & collaboration, Policies & rules, Threat policies, Preset security policies.
Turn on Standard protection for all recipients, and Strict for high-risk users.

checks.title: Attack simulation training is in use
checks.whyItMatters: Phishing simulations show who would click, and train them before a real attack does.
checks.minimum: At least one simulation in the last 90 days.
fix: In Microsoft Defender, open Email & collaboration, Attack simulation training.
Schedule a simulation with training for people who click.
